title: CareNow
tagline: Online doctors for small town families
pitch: You are building an app that connects families in small cities to a trusted doctor in minutes, in Hindi. You have ₹2 crore from angel investors and a few doctor friends. In about two years you must reach 50,000 monthly users, earn as much as you spend each month, and keep families' trust.

stages.title: Find the real problem
stages.situation: You want to make it easy for families in small towns to see a good doctor. You have one month to understand why it's hard today.

options.label: Run a WhatsApp survey of 3,000 people
options.outcome: Most say they want 'specialist doctors' and 'cheaper medicines'.
options.lesson: Surveys tell you what people wish for, not what they actually do when someone is ill at 10 PM.

later.note: Users who joined for specialists rarely needed one. The everyday need was never solved.

options.label: Spend 3 weeks at chemist shops and clinics in Indore and Nashik
options.outcome: You see the real pain: a 3 hour wait for a 3 minute visit, and the chemist acting as the doctor when the clinic is closed.
options.lesson: Seeing the real journey shows where time and trust are lost. That's where to start.

options.label: Copy a big city doctor app
options.outcome: You save a month, but small town families use phones, money and doctors differently.
options.lesson: A product that works for one group can fail for another. Understand your users before copying.

stages.title: Pick your first users
stages.situation: Who do you build for first?

options.label: Parents of young children in 3 small cities
options.detail: Kids fall ill often, parents worry most.
options.outcome: Fever at night is common and stressful. Parents talk to each other constantly.
options.lesson: A frequent, emotional need builds habit and word of mouth fast.

options.label: Anyone with any health problem, all over India
options.outcome: You need doctors for every specialty and language. Costs pile up.
options.lesson: Trying to treat everything first makes the product average for everyone.

options.label: People wanting weight loss and skin care plans
options.outcome: Sign ups come fast, mostly from Instagram, and leave as fast.
options.lesson: A trendy need can bring quick money but weak loyalty.

later.note: Most weight loss users quit after a month. A new influencer brand took the rest.

stages.title: Build the first version
stages.situation: You have two months to launch.

options.label: Video and phone calls with 30 verified child doctors, 8 AM to midnight, in Hindi
options.outcome: Parents get a doctor in 10 minutes, in their language, at night.
options.lesson: An MVP should do the core job very well for the first users. Here that's a trusted doctor, fast.

options.label: A full hospital app: all specialists, lab tests, medicines, insurance
options.outcome: It looks impressive and is confusing. Most specialists get zero calls.
options.lesson: Building everything before you know what's used burns money.

options.label: An AI symptom checker with no doctor
options.outcome: People love the speed. It sometimes gets serious cases wrong.
options.lesson: In health, a wrong answer can hurt someone. Speed is never worth that risk.

later.note: Your symptom checker told a parent a child's fever was mild. It was dengue. The story is in the news.

options.label: ₹149 per consult, or ₹999 a year for the whole family
options.outcome: Many families buy the yearly plan after the first good call.
options.lesson: A fair price plus a plan for repeat users turns one visit into a relationship.

options.label: Free consults for the first 3 months
options.outcome: Users pour in. So do doctor bills.
options.lesson: Free with no plan to charge trains users that your product is worth nothing.

later.note: You started charging. Many users went back to the free chemist advice.

options.label: ₹499 per consult, premium doctors only
options.outcome: Few families can afford it for a child's cold.
options.lesson: Price must match what your users can pay and how often they need you.

stages.title: Launch
stages.situation: How do you get your first big wave of families?

options.label: Partner with 100 local chemists: they book a call for customers
options.detail: Go where people already ask for help.
options.outcome: Chemists recommend you to worried parents every evening.
options.lesson: A trusted local partner is the best channel for a trust-heavy product.

options.label: ₹30 lakh on Facebook and YouTube ads
options.outcome: Installs jump across India, far beyond your 3 cities and Hindi doctors.
options.lesson: Ads that reach people you can't serve well yet waste money.

later.note: Most users from the ads needed doctors you didn't have. They never came back.

options.label: Referral: free consult for both families
options.outcome: School WhatsApp groups spread it.
options.lesson: Referrals bring users like your best users.

stages.title: First week experience
stages.situation: Many parents sign up but panic and call the local clinic when a child is ill. What do you fix?

options.label: A 1-tap 'Talk to a doctor now' button and a follow-up call next day
options.detail: Make the first visit easy and caring.
options.outcome: Parents feel looked after. They call you first next time.
options.lesson: The first good experience and a small caring touch build the habit.

options.label: Push health tips 3 times a day
options.outcome: People mute the app. Some tips scare them.
options.lesson: Unwanted messages from a health app feel like fear-selling.

options.label: Cashback on medicines for opening the app daily
options.outcome: Opens rise. Real consults don't.
options.lesson: Reward the action that matters, not app opens.

stages.title: Choose your north star
stages.situation: Your team needs one number to chase every week.

options.label: Consults where the family's problem was solved, by follow-up check
options.outcome: Teams work on doctor quality, wait time and follow-ups.
options.lesson: A good north star measures the value users actually get.

options.label: App downloads
options.outcome: Marketing wins, care doesn't.
options.lesson: Downloads say nothing about health outcomes.

options.label: Number of consults
options.outcome: Doctors are pushed to keep calls short and book repeat visits.
options.lesson: Counting activity can reward the wrong behaviour. More visits isn't better health.

stages.title: Grow the team
stages.situation: You have 12,000 families. Who do you hire?

options.label: A senior medical head and a doctor quality team
options.outcome: Prescriptions are checked, doctors are trained, mistakes drop.
options.lesson: In health, medical quality is the product.

options.label: 15 sales callers to sell yearly plans
options.outcome: Sales rise. So do complaints about pushy calls.
options.lesson: Pushy selling in health feels like taking advantage of fear.

later.note: Families shared recordings of callers saying 'your child could get seriously ill without our plan'. Refunds are piling up.

options.label: Stay lean, founders handle doctor scheduling
options.outcome: You save money but the founders are exhausted.
options.lesson: Burnout is a real cost.

later.note: Missed doctor shifts left parents waiting an hour at night.

stages.title: Raise money
stages.situation: Investors are interested. How much do you raise?

options.label: ₹10 crore, promise 50 cities and all specialties
options.outcome: Huge cash, huge expectations.
options.lesson: Growing before the core works copies your losses everywhere.

later.note: To keep your promise, you hired hundreds of specialists who sat idle. Costs exploded.

options.label: ₹3 crore from doctors and health founders
options.outcome: Enough runway, and investors who know medicine and its rules.
options.lesson: Smart money brings advice, not just cash.

options.label: Don't raise. Aim for profit.
options.outcome: You stay careful, but growth slows.
options.lesson: Not raising is valid, but you need a clear path to profit.

stages.title: Build a growth engine
stages.situation: You want growth that keeps going on its own. What do you build?

options.label: Medicine delivery from partner chemists after each consult
options.detail: Finish the job, and chemists earn too.
options.outcome: Families get medicine in an hour. Chemists earn more and recommend you more.
options.lesson: A loop where partners earn when users succeed keeps growing by itself.

options.label: TV ads on news channels
options.outcome: A big spike, mostly from cities you don't serve.
options.lesson: Expensive spikes don't build lasting growth.

later.note: Most TV sign ups found no doctor in their language and left.

options.label: Add 10 new specialties
options.outcome: Users grow, but most new specialists get few calls.
options.lesson: New categories bring growth and new costs.

stages.title: Earn more per family
stages.situation: You need more money per family. What do you try?

options.label: Ads from medicine brands in the app
options.outcome: Money comes in. Some parents wonder if doctors are pushed to prescribe those brands.
options.lesson: In health, ads raise doubts about advice. Keep them far from the doctor's choice.

options.label: Raise the yearly plan to ₹1,999
options.outcome: Revenue jumps, many families don't renew.
options.lesson: Price rises must match the value families feel.

options.label: Home lab tests booked after a consult
options.outcome: Slow start, then doctors' test requests turn into bookings.
options.lesson: Selling the next step of the same journey builds margin.

later.note: Home lab tests took off. Margins on them are double.

stages.title: A giant enters
stages.situation: A big pharmacy app launches free doctor consults with medicine orders.

options.label: Make your consults free too
options.outcome: Users stay, but you are burning cash fast.
options.lesson: Price wars favour the player with the most money.

later.note: The free consult war ended. Your cash is gone, and bargain hunters moved on.

options.label: Ignore price. Double down on your child doctors and follow-ups
options.outcome: Some try the giant. Its doctors rush to sell medicines.
options.lesson: Compete on what users trust you for.

later.note: Parents came back, saying the free doctors just wanted to sell medicine.

options.label: Pivot to software for clinics
options.outcome: Families feel abandoned. The team is confused.
options.lesson: Running from competition throws away what you built.

stages.title: A crisis
stages.situation: A doctor on your app gave a wrong dose. The child is fine now, but the parent's post is viral.

options.label: Apologise, cover the hospital bill, add a second check on every prescription
options.detail: Own it and fix the system.
options.outcome: It costs money, but families see you take safety seriously.
options.lesson: Handling a crisis openly can build more trust than you had before.

options.label: Send a legal notice to the parent
options.outcome: This becomes the bigger story.
options.lesson: Fighting a worried parent in public is a disaster.

options.label: Say it was the doctor's fault, not the app's
options.outcome: Users see it as dodging. Your other doctors are upset.
options.lesson: Users hold you responsible for everyone on your platform.

stages.title: Doctors want a better deal
stages.situation: Your doctors say pay per call is too low and night shifts are tiring. Some are leaving.

options.label: Raise pay, add fair shift limits, show doctor ratings
options.outcome: Costs rise, but doctors stay and care is better.
options.lesson: In a marketplace, both sides need a fair deal.

options.label: Replace them with cheaper, less experienced doctors
options.outcome: Families notice the difference within weeks.
options.lesson: Cutting quality in health costs more than it saves.

options.label: Pay doctors more for high follow-up ratings
options.outcome: Top doctors earn more. Some others feel judged.
options.lesson: Paying for outcomes can work if it's fair.

stages.title: The road to profit
stages.situation: Investors want a clear path to profit before the next round.

options.label: Drop the 3 least used specialties and night shifts in small cities
options.outcome: Some families leave, but costs fall a lot.
options.lesson: Cutting losing parts focuses the business on what works.

options.label: Expand to 20 new cities now
options.outcome: Big new costs before the core is profitable.
options.lesson: Expanding to escape problems usually multiplies them.

options.label: Raise consult price 5%
options.outcome: A bit more revenue. Some families leave.
options.lesson: Small price changes add up, but watch trust and growth.

events.title: Dengue season
events.situation: Dengue cases spike. Calls triple overnight.

options.label: Add doctors early and share free prevention tips
options.outcome: Families get help fast and tell others.
options.lesson: Prepare for known peaks. They're when users judge you.

options.label: Run as normal
options.outcome: Wait times hit 2 hours.
options.lesson: Failing at the peak hurts trust the most.

events.title: Video calls fail
events.situation: Your video provider goes down for an evening.

options.label: Switch to phone calls and tell families
options.outcome: Consults continue.
options.lesson: Have a backup for the tools you depend on.

options.label: Wait for it to come back
options.outcome: Worried parents wait with no answers.
options.lesson: Silence in a health app feels like abandonment.

events.title: A rival poaches your medical head
events.situation: Your medical head has an offer at double the pay.

options.label: Counter-offer with equity
options.outcome: They stay.
options.lesson: Key people are worth investing in.

options.label: Let them go and promote from within
options.outcome: Quality slips for a while.
options.lesson: Losing key people has a cost.

events.title: New rules for online doctors
events.situation: The government publishes strict rules on online prescriptions and patient data.

options.label: Follow them right away and tell users
options.outcome: Some extra cost, but families feel safe.
options.lesson: Following rules early builds trust.

options.label: Wait and see
options.outcome: A complaint becomes a fine and a news story.
options.lesson: Rules for patient safety are a floor, not an option.
